# quick :: rv_palm_rapeoil

**Q:** Set palm oil against rapeseed oil for me -- whose stocks position moved more this year, and how do the two read against each other now?

**TL;DR.** On the one stock comparison this page carries, both Chinese inventories built over the window, and rapeseed oil in China moved the larger amount  --  a build of 121,000 MT [N4] against 19,800 MT [N3] for palm  --  even though palm still carries the bigger level at 724,100 MT [N1] versus 412,000 MT [N2] for rapeseed oil, read through June 2026. Both legs loosen rather than tighten, so the stocks signal alone points toward softer prices on both, with the tie-breaking pull coming from elsewhere: Malaysian closing stocks are also building [N61][N67], while the EU rapeseed balance is being loosened by record Black Sea seed supply.

**Why.** ## Mechanism
The two are one complex joined by substitution: palm sets the floor of the vegetable-oil stack, and a higher palm price lifts rapeseed oil with it; rapeseed oil and soyoil fill gaps in the same bottling and biodiesel book. So stocks on either side transmit  --  rising inventories on one leg loosen the whole substitution pool, not just its own market.

- **Palm side.** Rising Malaysian and Indonesian month-end inventories are the model's high-confidence loosening channel; Malaysian closing stocks were 2.62832 MMT [N61], up +0.0845 MMT from the prior month [N66] and rising in each of the last 4 months [N67]. That is a demand-deficient build and it pressures the nearby.
- **Rapeseed side.** MATIF has no comparable month-end stock print here; what the record shows instead is the supply that fills it  --  Russian rapeseed at 7 MMT [N5], 99th percentile of its own record [N7], and Ukrainian rapeseed at 4.35 MMT [N14], 96th percentile [N16]. Both are declared to move MATIF in the opposite direction at high confidence. EU stocks-to-use reads 9.42 % [N20], past the desk's own ample line, though falling over the last marketing year.
- **What offsets.** Crude is the shared support: the Brent five-year z-score sits at 0.507294 z [N59][N60], up +0.5124 z on the month [N64][N65], which improves biodiesel economics on both legs. The corpus documents exactly this substitution logic  --  when palm ran expensive, rapeseed oil's biodiesel feedstock call strengthened [E11].

## The record
- China ending stocks, palm oil 724,100 MT [N1] and rapeseed oil 412,000 MT [N2], read through June 2026; the window changes are 19,800 MT [N3] and 121,000 MT [N4]. Rapeseed oil made the larger move; palm holds the larger level. Both built.
- EU crush demand at 25.1 MMT [N11], 91st percentile [N13] but falling over the last marketing year  --  the demand leg that would absorb seed is easing, not strengthening.
- Palm-belt dryness reads 0.16 z [N47], 72nd percentile [N49], rising in each of the last two months; the ocean temperature index reads -0.39 degC [N50], 35th percentile [N52]. Both are declared to lift palm in the same direction on a two-to-four-quarter biological lag, so they are next year's supply story, not this quarter's.
- Indonesian export policy reads on one series across the levy, domestic-obligation and ban names  --  23.5 MMT [N41], 87th percentile [N43], falling over the last marketing year. That is one reading under three names, not three confirmations.
- MATIF rapeseed front 2026M11 settled at 554.25 EUR/t on 2026-09-15 [N53], +19.5 over twenty-one sessions [N56] but -3.75 over five [N55]. No CME palm oil price row is served this session  --  the front delivery month could not be named, so I make no cross-board price comparison, and in any case the two settle in different currencies.
- Dated documents are thin and old for this pair: the newest behind this answer is 2026-03-31, and the substitution mechanics I lean on date to 2023 and 2022. The number rows run through 2026-09-15, the board price tape through 2026-09-15, and the newest dated document is far older than either.

## Where the record disagrees
The stocks legs and the weather legs point opposite ways on palm, at the same high confidence. Building Malaysian inventories [N61][N67] loosen the balance now; dryness in the palm belt [N47] and the ocean index [N50] tighten it two to four quarters out. Two of the six drivers the price-supportive palm supply-squeeze pattern names are among this board's largest moves, and that pattern's own threshold is three  --  so it is not armed. My read: the near-dated stock build dominates the current quarter and the weather legs are a right-tail risk for later, not a present tightener. note that reading and the autumn-establishment reading are one series printed under two names, so count them once.

## Cross-commodity
Palm against rapeseed oil on the Chinese stock comparison, read through June 2026:
- Palm oil in China: 724,100 MT [N1], change over the window 19,800 MT [N3].
- Rapeseed oil in China: 412,000 MT [N2], change over the window 121,000 MT [N4].

These are Chinese commercial inventories, not world balance sheets, so read them as one buyer's positioning and not as a global stocks-to-use comparison. Rapeseed oil made the larger build from the smaller base  --  that is the leg whose local availability improved most, and it points to softer relative rapeseed-oil pull in the Chinese cooking-oil stack. The same loud state is declared on two other markets the model tracks: DCE palm olein, which depends on the Malaysian crude palm price it is fractionated from and carries the same-direction sign, and ICE raw sugar, where the Indian rupee reading is declared in the opposite direction at zero to two quarters. The rupee itself reads 95.96 per USD [N17], 99th percentile [N19], declared to move palm in the opposite direction  --  a weaker rupee rations the largest buyer's palm purchases at the margin, which compounds the stock build rather than offsetting it.

## What to watch
- **Ukrainian rapeseed supply** [N14]  --  the top decile of its own record, on the high side. This is the leg feeding the EU crush and pressuring MATIF; it reads wrong if the next print returns the series toward the middle of its own record.
- **EU growing-season moisture** [N32]  --  one of three drivers of the price-supportive EU supply-shock pattern currently among the largest moves, against that pattern's own threshold of three. The declared lag window, counted from that reading's date, runs 2026-07-31 to 2027-01-31. It reads wrong if one of the pattern's named drivers turns and the count falls back under threshold.
- **Indonesian export policy** [N41]  --  the same reading is declared on fourteen other markets, all in the same direction, the nearest being DCE palm olein at zero to one quarter, high confidence. A move here has to be priced on markets this note is not about. It reads wrong if that market's declared edge carries no sign, in which case the reach is a count and not a direction.
